reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm target engagement for either CTLA-4 or VEGF. Cannot assess whether ipilimumab engaged CTLA-4 or bevacizumab engaged VEGF. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to assess downstream biological changes from checkpoint blockade or angiogenesis inhibition. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (OS) clearly failed - HR 0.94 (p=0.383) shows no benefit from adding bevacizumab to ipilimumab. Secondary endpoints (PFS, response rates) also failed to show benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Trial appears adequately powered (N=169) and conducted over appropriate timeframe (260 weeks). Higher grade 3-5 AE rate in combination arm (58% vs 39%) suggests both drugs were delivered, but this didn't translate to efficacy benefit. The failure appears to be that the combination hypothesis (checkpoint blockade + angiogenesis inhibition) did not improve outcomes over checkpoint blockade alone.

failure_modes.evidence: While we cannot confirm target engagement or pathway modulation due to lack of biomarker data, the combination arm showed higher toxicity (58% vs 39% grade 3-5 AEs) suggesting drug delivery occurred, yet all efficacy endpoints failed to improve. This suggests the assumed biological synergy between checkpoint blockade and angiogenesis inhibition did not translate to clinical benefit.
